overview: The ETA-2 Actis Interceptor is a jedi interceptor whose service history spans Clone Wars (22–19 BBY). The sleek successor to the Delta-7, flown by Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker in the final days of the Clone Wars. Imperial archives, Rebel intelligence briefings, and Mandalorian shipyard records estimate total production at ~12,000 units, though wartime losses and black-market refits make exact counts difficult to verify.
history:
Design bureaus first drafted the ETA-2 Actis Interceptor during the political tensions that defined Clone Wars (22–19 BBY). Engineers prioritised capabilities suited to its role as a jedi interceptor, balancing armour, manoeuvrability, and crew requirements against the industrial capacity of the factions that ordered it into production.

As fleet doctrine evolved, the ETA-2 Actis Interceptor entered front-line service in convoy escort, planetary assault, and deep-space patrol missions. The sleek successor to the Delta-7, flown by Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker in the final days of the Clone Wars. Veterans praised its reliability under fire while analysts debated whether mass production at ~12,000 units diluted quality control across shipyard lines.

Major campaigns cemented the vessel's reputation — whether as a terror weapon, a rebel lifeline, or a smuggler's last hope. Battle damage reports show the jedi interceptor could absorb punishment that would destroy lighter craft, though attrition rates climbed sharply during the bloodiest years of galactic war.

In the modern era, surviving hulls appear in private collections, museum orbits, and covert fleets. Restorers hunt spare parts across scrap worlds while historians argue the ETA-2 Actis Interceptor symbolises the industrial scale of conflict more than any single battle honour.
significance:
The ETA-2 Actis Interceptor illustrates how shipwright traditions and wartime desperation combine to shape galactic warfare. Its jedi interceptor layout influenced successor designs long after production lines fell silent.

Approximately ~12,000 units hulls served during Clone Wars (22–19 BBY), making the class one of the most visible symbols of its faction's naval power. Colour markings and unit insignia turned anonymous factory output into icons recognised across holonet broadcasts.

For engineers and tacticians, the ETA-2 Actis Interceptor remains a case study in trade-offs between firepower, crew survival, and maintenance — lessons still taught at academies from Coruscant to Mandalore.
